item.title: California Democrat Rep. Gomez resigns following ethics report on sexual misconduct allegations
item.description:
Congress
California Democrat Rep. Gomez resigns following ethics report on sexual misconduct allegations
November 23, 20265:29 PM ET
By
Sam Gringlas
U.S. Rep. Jimmy Gomez, seen here at a Congressional hearing in March, announced Monday that he would resign following a report from the House Ethics committee on allegations of sexual misconduct.
Heather Diehl/Getty Images North America
hide caption
toggle caption i
Heather Diehl/Getty Images North America
Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says he is resigning from Congress after a bipartisan investigation released Monday found "substantial evidence" he engaged in sexual misconduct toward a House staffer.
The House Ethics Committee concluded Gomez violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances and engaging in unwelcome sexual conduct towards a House staffer and disregarding the power imbalance inherent in his relationship with House staffers."
The report also says the behavior could constitute criminal sexual assault.
Gomez has served in Congress since 2017 representing parts of Los Angeles. He lost reelection this fall to fellow Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres. California uses a system where the top two vote-getters no matter the party advance to the general election. Gomez says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.

item.title: Mending relationships over the holidays? Considering a truce? NPR wants to know
item.description:
News
Mending relationships over the holidays? Considering a truce? NPR wants to know
November 23, 20263:53 PM ET
Lauren Hodges
Mark Makela/REUTERS
The divisive American political climate over the last few years has been splintering relationships. Whether you've blocked a high school buddy on social media or cut off a relative, there are some issues that may have felt too big to ignore.
But with the midterms over and holiday season getting started, there might be an incentive to re-start the conversation. If you're considering a truce this season or even a full amends, we want to hear about it.
Fill out the form below, and an NPR producer may reach out to you and your loved one for a conversation.
We will not use your submission in our story until we have communicated with you and obtained your consent to use the details that will be published.

item.description:
World
Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
Updated November 23, 20262:57 PM ET
Originally published November 23, 20265:16 AM ET
By
The Associated Press
In this image made from video provided by Russian Defense Ministry Press Service on Sunday, July 16, 2023, a Russian navy corvette Merkury attends naval military exercises in the Baltic Sea.
Russian Defense Ministry Press Service/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Russian Defense Ministry Press Service/AP
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.
Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X.
